summary: Independent Q6 inspection finds a substantive, stateful and operationally coherent JetStream continuity system rather than LOC padding. The solver-visible entrypoint reaches the defect-bearing ContinuityEngine through starter_cli, which deliberately binds the operator CLI to environment/continuity/continuity/engine.py. That engine participates in real NATS JetStream publication, generation control, consumer effects, reconciliation, replay, recovery fencing and retention while delegating durable operations to a substantial SQLite store and live JetStream integration layer. The major subsystems have distinct responsibilities and share event identity, generation, archive, checkpoint, replay, lease and retention state, creating genuine cross-component partial-fix traps. Incident evidence is internally consistent with the seeded operational topology. The reference repair replaces the same engine module used by continuityctl and repairs those operational invariants rather than introducing a bypass or alternate result-producing path. No HIGH toy-logic or padding risk was identified.

evidence.observation: Q6 requires independent assessment of reachability, material branching/state/error handling, subsystem diversity, cross-component interactions, removal impact and padding risk; raw LOC or Complexity Governor PASS is insufficient.

The Q6 method requires tracing entrypoints, major-module reachability, distinct responsibilities, clone/wrapper risk, cross-module invariants, a roughly 25-percent removal test and data/state consumption.
The normal operator entrypoint executes python -m continuity.starter_cli, establishing a real solver-visible command path rather than a test-only entrypoint.

starter_cli imports ContinuityEngine from .engine and assigns it into cli.ContinuityEngine before invoking cli.main. It also applies the runtime SQLite schema extension. This makes the defect-bearing engine module reachable through continuityctl rather than dead code.

The CLI exposes durable database initialization, health/status, reconciliation, generation approval, replay planning/execution, lease operations, retention, three-server lab lifecycle, archive synchronization, consumer execution, reset and final verification. These commands instantiate the patched ContinuityEngine and connect it to shared SQLite and NATS runtime state.

The runtime contains genuine NATS/JetStream integration: connection pooling, domain-aware API requests, stream and consumer administration, message retrieval, publish acknowledgements, pull consumers, archive synchronization, topology bootstrap and lifecycle management of separate east, west and hub nats-server processes.

The persistence layer uses transactional SQLite/WAL state and models event journals, publish attempts, origin generations, archive identity, consumer effects, checkpoints, replay state, leases, retention state, reconciliation findings and operator actions. Operations enforce identity/idempotency and state-transition constraints rather than serving constant outputs.

The base continuity controller provides substantial shared topology, stream-policy, event-generation, publishing, consumer-effect and other operational behavior. engine.py specializes this implementation instead of replacing a toy shell.

The inherited controller contains interacting starter manifestations in real workflows: attempt-scoped message identity, publication state handling, automatic generation confirmation, consumer dispatch/effect/checkpoint ordering, count/sequence-based reconciliation, broad replay ranges, fencing behavior and retention safe-sequence calculation. These defects affect shared persistent state and normal operator commands.

The environment installs a real pinned nats-server binary, nats-py and SQLite tooling, initializes durable state, preserves runtime directories and exposes the continuity package as the normal application environment.

The production-authenticity specification identifies a 10,000-20,000 row event journal with variance across regions, devices, sites, event types, payload sizes, priorities, publish states and consumer roles. Independent code inspection found corresponding branches and state consumers for these dimensions; they are not merely opaque filler fields.

The incident handoff ties a regional disconnect to locally accepted edge telemetry, missing archive identities, JetStream/application checkpoint disagreement, duplicate effects, replay holds and unsafe cleanup. Those symptoms correspond directly to state and logic implemented by the production modules.

The captured topology describes two 6,000-message edge streams, an 11,395-message hub archive, source lag, two required consumer checkpoint discrepancies and cleanup watermarks. It also embeds a west-source domain mismatch and unsafe cleanup sequences that are operationally meaningful inputs to topology/generation/reconciliation/retention logic.

The Oracle installs a repaired engine.py and continuity configuration into the same /app/continuity package used by continuityctl, compiles the normal production modules and invokes continuityctl verify. It does not replace continuityctl, patch the verifier, synthesize passing reports directly or introduce an alternate test-only execution path.

The reference repair materially changes live domain behavior: stable event message identity, generation approval semantics and origin observations, once-only consumer dispatch, effect/ack ordering, identity-based reconciliation, missing-only replay ranges with overlap detection, monotonic fencing epochs, exact fence validation, retention bounded by archive/consumer/replay watermarks and consistency-aware consumer health.

PARTIAL_FIX_TRAPS: Changing publish retry handling without stable event identity can still duplicate JetStream messages or downstream effects after uncertain acknowledgements.
Treating a stream sequence reset as ordinary progress can invalidate generation identity even if publication itself is repaired.
Reconciliation based only on counts or high-water marks can appear converged while specific event identities or metadata remain wrong.
Replay selection depends on reconciliation identity, generation authority and overlap handling; repairing only the publisher leaves unsafe replay scope.
Consumer correctness spans durable effect idempotency, dispatch cardinality, application effect checkpoints, JetStream acknowledgement ordering and redelivery behavior.

Retention safety is jointly constrained by contiguous archive progress, the slowest required consumer, active replay pins, minimum journal age and holds; using only archive progress can destroy recoverability.
Recovery ownership depends on lease expiry plus monotonic fence epochs and exact token validation; fixing acquisition without assertion semantics still permits stale workers.

The runtime topology, archive synchronizer and stored origin/source metadata interact, so configuration mistakes can surface later as reconciliation/generation anomalies rather than simple startup failures.
role_output.REMOVAL_TEST: Removing approximately 25% of the substantive core cannot be done without materially reducing behavior. Removing the store's generation/archive/effect/checkpoint/replay/lease/retention portions eliminates durable safety invariants; removing runtime.py eliminates actual JetStream administration, publication, consumer and archive synchronization; removing engine/policy portions eliminates the incident's reconciliation/replay/fencing/retention and effect semantics; removing the operator binding/CLI disconnects those behaviors from the solver-visible workflow. There is no comparably large removable block whose deletion would leave the claimed system behavior intact.
